metadata.description: Google Slides deck generation: template-driven, from-scratch, Scalar product and proposal workflows, plus template creation (template-forge), reusable single-slide content templates (slide-template-creator), a rendered catalog of all 43 page patterns, B2B influence and discovery maps, draw.io diagrams, an optional visual-QA skill, PPTX export, and line-item spreadsheets (Excel / Google Spreadsheet) for estimates and BOMs, on a shared Python engine; CLI messages default to English (GSLIDES_LANG=ja for Japanese); templates record their image slots (imageSlots) so pictures land where the design intends and AI images are drawn for the slot's shape, and body text supports per-line emphasis, links to another slide or deck, and a body-fit check; the offline audits also catch lines running across text; an existing deck's empty image frames can be filled with generated pictures; generation is measurably faster — one batchUpdate instead of 500-request chunks, no requests that merely restate API defaults, local images uploaded in parallel, and thumbnail fetching parallelised within the API's 60-per-minute quota; plus a Scalar Account Executive kit: a per-customer sales ledger (account.json) that records what is confirmed versus assumed, who decides, which stage gates are met with customer-side evidence, and what is still unknown — rendered as an activity-plan deck whose URL never changes, filed under 'AE name / customer name' in Drive

plugins.name: slide-forge
plugins.description: Generate Google Slides decks with Python + the Slides API. Twelve skills on one shared engine: google-slides-template (generate from a registered master template with interactive intake and spec validation), google-slides (from-scratch decks via a blank template spec path or a code-first deckkit path with offline layout validation), scalar-product-slides (Scalar Inc. company/product deck workflow), scalar-proposal-slides (customer-challenge-driven Scalar solution proposals with challenge-to-product mapping, 3-environment architecture diagrams, and a BOM with quantities and monthly costs), drawio-diagrams (dense cloud architecture / data-flow diagrams authored as draw.io files and exported to PNG headlessly), slide-qa (thumbnail-based visual QA of a generated deck — optional at generation time, default on, with cleanup of the local QA files when done), pptx-export (export a generated deck to PowerPoint .pptx as a delivery format — chosen at intake or run standalone on any deck URL, with automatic fallback past the 10MB export limit and archival in the deck's Drive folder), and spreadsheets (line-item Excel / Google Spreadsheet deliverables — estimates, BOMs, cost breakdowns — from one JSON spec with typed columns, real formulas for amounts and subtotal/tax/total, offline validation, and in-place updates that preserve the Spreadsheet URL; the companion to a proposal deck's cost slide), and template-forge (create and register a brand-new template/master from a design spec — brand colors, fonts, logo, footer — by restyling a base master's layouts via the API, with deterministic role assignment and bundled design presets), and slide-template-creator (create and register reusable single-slide content templates — one page pattern such as SWOT, cohort retention or a conversion funnel, with semantic input slots that are type- and length-checked offline, a worked example per template, and a per-pack catalog deck for visual QA — stored under slide-templates/ and independent of Google Slides masters). Includes charts, business-framework figures, pictogram and cloud-vendor icon libraries, AI image generation, and parallel per-page spec authoring for large decks. The /forge command runs the whole pipeline (skill routing → intake → outline approval → validation → generation → optional visual QA → cleanup → report) as one continuous flow. Script CLI messages are English by default; set GSLIDES_LANG=ja for Japanese (generated deck/spreadsheet content is unaffected). Figure families include event-announcement parts (overview, timetable, speakers, venue/online/hybrid access panels) for seminar and conference decks. A rendered pattern catalog (references/slide-pattern-catalog.md) shows all 43 page patterns in 8 groups — one image per pattern with when to use it and the figures type names to write — so a deck can be planned by pointing at a picture instead of reading the spec schema. Side-by-side comparison is no longer limited to two columns: comparison takes any number of options, draws the connecting arrows only when the columns are a progression rather than alternatives, and can highlight one recommended option; before_after is now its two-column case. b2b-account-maps builds the two maps a B2B software deal turns on — an influence map of the buying committee on 影響力 × 賛否, and a discovery map that colours each MEDDPICC item by whether it is confirmed, partly known, or still an assumption — plus the buying committee table, the approval path, the pain chain from a floor-level task to the metric it moves, and the list of gaps with who to ask and by when. Its six page templates ship as the b2b-sales pack under slide-templates/. The maps are internal working artifacts, not customer-facing pages: they record judgements about named individuals. Templates now record where they want pictures (imageSlots: PICTURE placeholders, empty image frames left in a layout, and frames the bundled slides reuse); a deck spec omits x/y/w/h and the image lands in the frame, with a warning when one is placed elsewhere. An aiImage headed for a slot is generated for that slot's shape — the closest aspect ratio the model can produce, plus a prompt instruction naming the edges and percentage the fill will crop, so the subject is composed to survive it — and fills the frame instead of letterboxing inside it. Body text takes per-line roles (heading / strong / note, styled by the template's bodyRoles) and inline **emphasis**, so a long body no longer reads as a wall of uniform text, and --dry-run estimates the body height and warns before it overflows. Body lines also take inline links written as [text](target) — [text](#12) for another slide in the same deck, [text](https://…) for another deck or an external page — styled by bodyRoles.link (accent + underline) so they read as clickable, which makes appendix decks and cross-deck navigation practical. The offline audits now also report arrows, connectors and chart gridlines that run across text — a class of defect previously visible only in the thumbnails — while respecting draw order, so a line hidden under a shape painted over it is not flagged. Every deck-building script ships a --dry-run that runs the full audit set without calling the API. image-slots fills the empty picture frames of an **existing** deck: it finds them the same three ways template registration does (PICTURE placeholders, empty image elements, frames the deck reuses), draws each picture for that frame's shape, and places it filling the frame — standalone on any deck URL, including decks slide-forge did not generate, with no registered template required. It draws the subject from each slide title and, by default, only fills frames the template actually declares — frames merely inferred from how other slides use pictures need --include-inferred. Every Drive call passes supportsAllDrives, so decks, folders, exports, version snapshots and spreadsheets all work on shared drives. --dry-run is fully offline: it no longer uploads images to Drive, and any interrupted run cleans up its temporary uploads on exit instead of leaving them shared with anyone who has the link (images.py --sweep-temp clears ones stranded by older versions). Generation time was profiled against the live API and cut on four fronts: batchUpdate requests now go out in as few batches as the 10MB body limit allows (splitting them is what was slow — 8,000 requests take 18.2s in 500-request chunks and 6.3s in one, and running batches concurrently is slower still, so it does not); requests that only restate a shape's post-createShape defaults are no longer sent at all (about 19% fewer requests on a real deck); local images upload in parallel in the background while the figures are drawn, with the createImage URLs filled in just before commit (a 10-image deck went 37.3s to 16.9s); and thumbnail fetching for visual QA runs concurrently under a self-imposed rate limit matching the Slides API's 60-expensive-reads-per-minute quota, so a 55-slide deck takes 10.5s instead of 55s without ever tripping a 429. Verified by pixel-comparing 89 slides rendered before and after: no visual difference. Two new skills implement the Scalar B2B sales standard for Account Executives. scalar-account-plan keeps one ledger per customer (accounts/<AE>/<customer>/account.json) as the source of truth — facts labelled said / observed / assumed, the buying committee, MEDDPICC status, the pain chain, BANT risk, the current stage's exit criteria with the customer-side evidence for each, and the open actions — and renders it as a nine-page activity plan. The deck is rebuilt in place: build_deck.py --into replaces every page of an existing deck instead of creating a new one, so the shared link an AE hands round keeps working while the contents stay current (it refuses a deck built from a different master, and prints the pre-edit revision so File > Version history can roll it back). What the ledger cannot answer becomes the output that matters: account_ledger.py gaps checks the playbook's ten review questions and turns every unanswered one into an action with a person to ask and a completion condition, carried over between runs and written as both a slide and Markdown for the CRM's Next Action field. scalar-ae-materials builds one visit's materials, routed by deal phase (0-6) x audience x purpose so the customer-facing one-pager, the internal visit plan, the WPS win plan and the Deal Desk packet are never the same file — with a pre-generation check that no judgement about a named individual, competitor weakness or unconfirmed figure leaks into anything a customer will read. account_workspace.py builds the Drive tree <root>/<AE name>/<customer name>/{00_活動計画, 01_顧客提示, 02_顧客提案, 90_社内} idempotently by exact-name match, remembering the root in config/sales.json. Eight page templates ship as the scalar-ae pack. The /account and /visit commands run the two workflows end to end. references/scalar/sales-playbook.md is the single source for the phases, gate IDs, the five material types and the ten checkpoints; the skills do not restate them.
